Next I'll find out why the network is down.The box is back on the network. Next I copy the tarball to Zone.I have Rob's tarball. It's in `~/code/storage/futon6/results-mark7-mark7rhgrh12v4-20260927/`, set out like the mark7master run:

- the `.tar.gz` (48 MB, uploaded by Rob on 28 September at 18:59);
- a `.sha256` file; the checksum matches the copy on metameso (`2c1b41fb…`);
- `extracted/`, with 13,502 files and 779 MB unpacked. It includes `eval-summary.md`, `eval-report.json` and `accretion-curve.html`.

Nobody changed the configuration; the box had been sending its network traffic to its old London address. It rebooted a few minutes after Rob's upload, onto a new kernel. On the way up it configured eth0 from `/etc/network/interfaces`, a 2020 file with the London address `178.79.174.58` from when the box was in London. The correct Chicago settings are in `/etc/systemd/network/05-eth0.network`, but systemd-networkd is disabled, so that file was never used. The box had apparently not rebooted since November 2025, so this setup hadn't been tested since.

I put 172.236.108.82 on eth0 by hand. The box and https://metameso.org are reachable again, but only until the next reboot. To make the fix survive a reboot, I'd enable systemd-networkd and disable the `networking` service. That's worth doing only if the old box is going to stay for a while. If you'd rather finish the migration and delete it, the manual fix is enough until then.
